title: Early construction noise exemption deferred; gas rates and BIA expansion advance
subtitle: Quarterly gas supply rates, Belmont BIA expansion, school bus zones, crossing guards, Oktoberfest noise exemption and youth climate grants
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee deferred a request from a developer to start construction at 6 a.m. at 641 King Street West. Staff had recommended denial. The committee sent the matter to the September 30 Council meeting so the developer and staff can report on how they will consult neighbours.

On utilities, the committee recommended raising the natural gas supply rate for Kitchener Utilities customers from 11.63 to 13.13 cents per cubic metre on November 1, 2024. It also recommended moving to quarterly supply-rate changes from 2025 and approved new delivery rates for January 1, 2025 {{vote:m6}}. It recommended starting the formal notice process for expanding the Belmont Business Improvement Area {{vote:m7}}.

Consent items covered new school bus loading zones, crossing guard changes, a noise exemption for Oktoberfest events, Youth Climate Action Fund agreements and Nominating Committee reappointments. These are recommendations that Council will consider later. After the meeting, the chair also noted that a staff variance report projects a surplus.

decisions.item: 641 King St W early-start noise exemption
decisions.detail: The committee deferred the request for a 6 a.m. construction start, which staff recommended denying, to the September 30 Council meeting so neighbourhood engagement can be planned with staff.

decisions.item: Natural gas supply and delivery rates
decisions.detail: The committee recommended raising the supply rate to 13.13 cents per cubic metre from November 1, 2024, allowing quarterly supply-rate changes from 2025, and approving the proposed delivery rates from January 1, 2025.
The committee recommended sending formal notice of the proposed boundary change to affected commercial property owners, which starts the process but does not yet expand the BIA.

decisions.item: School bus zones and crossing guards
decisions.detail: The committee recommended extending or adding school bus loading zones at several streets, removing one on Emerald Avenue, adding crossing guards on Huron Road and Thomas Slee Drive, and removing three others.
The committee recommended exempting Kitchener-Waterloo Oktoberfest Inc. events at various clubs from the noise by-law from September 27 to October 19, 2024.
The committee recommended authorizing the CAO and General Managers to sign agreements with Youth Climate Action Fund grant recipients.
The committee recommended reappointing the listed community organization representatives to the Nominating Committee for a term to November 14, 2026, and amending two related policies.

debate: A developer representative said the 6 a.m. start would finish the tower work about two months sooner, with limited quiet activities from 6 to 7 a.m. and no saws or hammering. The representative added that amenities could open by summer 2025 and noise monitoring had been done.

Councillors asked why the request came after 17 months of construction and why other projects have worked within the 7 a.m. start. They also noted that the developer had not yet contacted neighbours. The developer agreed that a deferral for engagement was fair.

Staff said the 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. construction noise hours have long been in place. They said by-law enforcement had already received early-start complaints about this site, and approval could set a precedent for other projects.

On gas rates, councillors questioned accountability from delegating supply changes to staff. Staff said supply is a pass-through cost, delivery rates stay with Council, Council can step in, and quarterly changes reduce sudden spikes. Council would be emailed about changes.

On the Belmont BIA, one councillor worried about the added levy on businesses and about including distant properties with no connection to the area. Staff said the levy would be on commercial assessment only, and Council could adjust the boundary in January. If more than one-third object, the process ends.
